newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Gulf Arab exchanges capitalised at $90.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab exchanges capitalised at $90.7 billion.

text.p: Total market capitalisation for stock exchanges in the six Gulf Arab states in 1996 was $90.7 billion, a report said.
Al-Shall economic consultants said in a joint study with Bahrain International Bank that the amount represented 42 percent of aggregated total gross domestic product for the six states in 1995.

Saudi Arabia recorded the highest capitalisation in 1996 with $45.9 billion followed by Kuwait $21.8 billion, United Arab Emirates $13.6 billion, Bahrain $4.9 billion, Oman $2.4 billion and Qatar $2.1 billion.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, is the most populous of the six and has the largest economy.
Al-Shall's report said Oman, which like Kuwait and Bahrain have trading floors, had the largest number of listed concerns on its stock exchange in 1996 -- 97 companies.
Saudi Arabia came second with 71, 60 in Kuwait, 34 in Bahrain, 27 in the UAE and Qatar had 18 listed firms in 1996.

The Kuwait Stock Exchange recorded the highest trading value in 1996 with $19.2 billion while in Saudi Arabia it was $6.8 billion -- 15 percent of the market's capital value and five percent of 1995 GDP -- the report said.
